chapters.title: Crypto-Assets Other Than ARTs or EMTs
Authorisation and Operating Conditions for CASPs
Prevention and Prohibition of Market Abuse

articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Lays down uniform rules for transparency and disclosure, authorisation and supervision of CASPs, and issuance of asset-referenced tokens and e-money tokens

articles.title: Scope
articles.requirement: Applies to persons engaged in issuance, offer to the public, and admission to trading of crypto-assets, and to CASPs in the Union; exclusions for financial instruments, deposits, etc.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines crypto-asset, asset-referenced token, e-money token, CASP, distributed ledger technology, crypto-asset service, utility token, and other key terms

articles.title: Offers to the public of crypto-assets other than asset-referenced tokens or e-money tokens
articles.requirement: No person shall offer crypto-assets to the public unless a white paper has been drafted, notified to the competent authority, and published; exemptions for small offers and qualified investors

articles.title: Content and form of the crypto-asset white paper
articles.requirement: White paper must contain information about the issuer, project, rights and obligations, underlying technology, risks; must be fair, clear, and not misleading; Annex I specifies format

articles.title: Marketing communications
articles.requirement: Marketing communications must be clearly identifiable, fair, clear, not misleading, and consistent with the crypto-asset white paper

articles.title: Notification of the crypto-asset white paper and of the marketing communications
articles.requirement: White paper and marketing communications must be notified to the competent authority of the home Member State at least 20 working days before publication

articles.title: Publication of the crypto-asset white paper and of the marketing communications
articles.requirement: White paper must be published on the issuer's website in machine-readable format and remain available for as long as the crypto-asset is held by the public

articles.title: Right of withdrawal
articles.requirement: Consumers have a right of withdrawal within 14 calendar days of their agreement to purchase crypto-assets directly from the issuer, without incurring any cost

articles.title: Authorisation
articles.requirement: No person shall offer ARTs to the public or seek admission to trading unless authorised by the competent authority; credit institutions exempt from separate authorisation but must notify

articles.title: Application for authorisation
articles.requirement: Application must include programme of operations, governance arrangements, reserve of assets details, custody arrangements, complaint handling, white paper, and wind-down plan

articles.title: Content and form of the crypto-asset white paper for asset-referenced tokens
articles.requirement: ART white paper must contain specific information per Annex II: detailed description of issuer, stabilisation mechanism, rights of holders, reserve composition, and redemption procedures

articles.title: Obligation to act honestly, fairly and professionally in the best interest of the holders of asset-referenced tokens
articles.requirement: ART issuers must act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interest of token holders and treat all holders equally unless the white paper provides for preferential treatment

articles.title: Governance arrangements
articles.requirement: ART issuers must have robust governance including clear organisational structure, well-defined lines of responsibility, effective risk management, internal control mechanisms, and fit and proper management

articles.title: Own funds requirements
articles.requirement: ART issuers must maintain own funds equal to the higher of EUR 350,000, 2% of the average reserve assets, or a quarter of fixed overheads of the preceding year

articles.title: Obligation to have a reserve of assets, and composition and management
articles.requirement: ART issuers must constitute and maintain a reserve of assets backing the token, invested in secure low-risk assets, segregated from the issuer's own assets

articles.title: Custody of reserve assets
articles.requirement: Reserve assets must be held in custody by credit institutions or authorised crypto-asset custodians ensuring segregation and availability for timely redemption

articles.title: Prohibition of granting interest
articles.requirement: Issuers of ARTs and CASPs shall not grant interest or any other benefit related to the length of time during which a holder holds asset-referenced tokens

articles.title: Classification of asset-referenced tokens as significant asset-referenced tokens
articles.requirement: EBA classifies ARTs as significant based on customer base size, value of issued tokens, number and value of transactions, cross-border activity, and interconnectedness with financial system

articles.title: Requirements for offers to the public and admission to trading of e-money tokens
articles.requirement: Only credit institutions or electronic money institutions authorised under Directive 2009/110/EC may issue e-money tokens to the public in the Union

articles.title: Issuance and redeemability of e-money tokens
articles.requirement: EMT issuers must issue at par value on receipt of funds and redeem at par value at any time at the holder's request, without charge beyond the cost necessary for the transaction

articles.title: Prohibition of granting interest
articles.requirement: Issuers of EMTs and CASPs shall not grant interest or any other benefit related to the length of time during which a holder holds e-money tokens

articles.title: Content and form of the crypto-asset white paper for e-money tokens
articles.requirement: EMT issuers must draw up and publish a white paper containing information specified in Annex III before offering EMTs to the public

articles.title: Classification of e-money tokens as significant e-money tokens
articles.requirement: EBA classifies EMTs as significant based on same criteria as significant ARTs; significant EMT issuers subject to additional requirements and direct EBA oversight

articles.title: Authorisation of crypto-asset service providers
articles.requirement: Only legal persons with registered office in a Member State may apply for CASP authorisation; must meet fit and proper, governance, prudential, and operational requirements

articles.title: Application for authorisation
articles.requirement: Application must include programme of operations, proof of own funds, governance arrangements, internal control mechanisms, ICT security policies, business continuity, and complaint handling

articles.title: Obligation to act honestly, fairly and professionally in the best interests of clients
articles.requirement: CASPs must act honestly, fairly, and professionally in the best interests of clients and provide fair, clear, and not misleading information

articles.title: Prudential requirements
articles.requirement: CASPs must maintain permanent minimum capital (EUR 50,000 to EUR 150,000 depending on services) or a quarter of fixed overheads of the preceding year, whichever is higher

articles.title: Governance arrangements
articles.requirement: CASPs must have robust governance including clear organisational structure, effective risk management, adequate internal control, and fit and proper management body members

articles.title: Providing custody and administration of crypto-assets on behalf of clients
articles.requirement: CASPs providing custody must establish custody policy, segregate client assets from own assets, ensure clients' assets are not used for own account, and return assets without undue delay

articles.title: Operation of a trading platform for crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs operating trading platforms must establish operating rules, admission criteria, transparent fee structures, and real-time publication of prices, volumes, and completed transactions

articles.title: Exchange of crypto-assets for funds or other crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs providing exchange services must establish a non-discriminatory commercial policy, publish firm prices or methodology for determining prices, and execute orders at quoted prices

articles.title: Providing advice on crypto-assets and providing portfolio management of crypto-assets
articles.requirement: CASPs providing advice or portfolio management must assess suitability, act in the client's best interest, provide periodic statements, and disclose conflicts of interest

articles.title: Scope of the rules on market abuse
articles.requirement: Market abuse rules apply to any transaction, order, or behaviour concerning crypto-assets admitted to trading or for which admission has been sought, regardless of where conducted

articles.title: Prohibition of insider dealing
articles.requirement: No person in possession of inside information shall use that information to acquire or dispose of crypto-assets, or recommend or induce another person to do so

articles.title: Prohibition of market manipulation
articles.requirement: No person shall engage in market manipulation including wash trading, spoofing, layering, dissemination of false or misleading information, or any other artifice to distort prices

articles.title: Prevention and detection of market abuse
articles.requirement: CASPs operating trading platforms must establish and maintain effective systems and procedures for prevention and detection of market abuse; report suspected abuse to competent authority

articles.title: Administrative penalties and other administrative measures
articles.requirement: Member States must provide for effective, proportionate, and dissuasive administrative penalties and measures for MiCA breaches; minimum powers for competent authorities

articles.title: Entry into force and application
articles.requirement: Entered into force 29 June 2023. Title III and IV (ARTs and EMTs) apply from 30 June 2024. Remainder applies from 30 December 2024
